items.title: Patient Monitoring (Intraoperative Standards)
items.summary: The 'Monitoring' heading (source_pdf_page 55 in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json, status UNRESOLVED) has NO corresponding node anywhere in toc_inventory.json's 59 chapter-A nodes - unlike the A.S01/A.S06 same-page merges, there was no existing node to split; the TOC-extraction pipeline dropped this heading entirely.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of pdf page 61 (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0061.json) confirms the heading text is 'Canadian Guidelines to the Practice of Anesthesia and Patient Monitoring', immediately followed on the same page by the confirmed body-heading match already recorded for node A.S03 ('Airway Management'). Represented as SU-A-07 with source_node_ids ['UNCATALOGUED:Monitoring@pdf61'] since no real toc_inventory.json node id exists to cite.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator should consider adding a corresponding node to toc_inventory.json for chapter A (between A.S02 and A.S03, pdf page 61) in a future TOC-extraction pass, since this confirms at least one heading is missing from the pipeline's output entirely (not merged, dropped) - the same class of gap that produced the ELOM reference-disclaimer reattribution case. Flagged informational/low-priority since chapter A's own crosswalk is unaffected (SU-A-07 is fully resolved and validated).

items.recommended_action: Coordinator/reviewer to confirm whether this WEAK secondary citation adds value or should be dropped in favor of the MODERATE 74-3 evidence alone.

items.title: Malignant Hyperthermia
items.summary: No MCC objective names malignant hyperthermia verbatim, despite it being one of the highest-yield, most classically board-tested facts in anesthesia. The best available anchor, 107-1 'Fever and hyperthermia' (MODERATE strength), only lists the mechanistically-analogous 'drug-induced syndromes (e.g., neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome)' in its causal_conditions, not MH itself. This is honestly documented in the crosswalk's mapping_rationale rather than forced to a false STRONG match.
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter A's own crosswalk (evidence is defensible at MODERATE); flagged for coordinator awareness in case future MCC objectives_registry.json updates add MH explicitly, or in case other chapters (e.g. Pediatrics, Surgery) encounter the same naming gap and a cross-chapter registry annotation would help.

items.title: References/Landmark-Trials merge pattern confirmed genuine (contrast with ELOM)
items.summary: CP.S06's merged_duplicate_headings field lists 'References' alongside 'Landmark Pharmacology Trials' (both indexed to TOC page CP14 / pdf 188), structurally identical in shape to the ELOM ELOM.S04 case where a 'References'-labelled node turned out to be a misattributed disclaimer paragraph rather than a genuine bibliography.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of body page 0188.json (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0188.json) confirms CP.S06's 'References' heading here genuinely IS a correctly-attributed, >30-entry chapter bibliography (author/journal/year citations throughout: e.g. Boyer, 'The serotonin syndrome', NEJM 2005; Busse et al., opioid-therapy guideline, CMAJ 2017), with no clinical/testable prose mixed in. items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk. Flagged for coordinator awareness that the same_page_toc_merge_protocol.md 'References' detection signal (step to check whether a References node is genuine or a misattribution) produces DIFFERENT outcomes across chapters - genuine in Chapter CP, misattributed in Chapter ELOM - confirming the protocol's per-chapter case-by-case verification requirement is doing real work and should not be shortcut in future chapters that show this same merge shape.

items.title: Opioid Therapy nested under Autonomic Physiology heading despite thematic mismatch
items.summary: CP.S04's same-page merge nests 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' as a third printed TOC sub-bullet under 'Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology' (alongside Parasympathetic/Sympathetic Nervous System), even though opioid-prescribing guideline content has no thematic connection to autonomic nervous system physiology.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of body pages 0185.json/0186.json confirms 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' is its own genuine, independently-bolded body heading, printed immediately after the Autonomic Physiology content ends (Table 3 / Figure 8) with no textual continuity between the two. Represented as its own separate study unit, SU-CP-16, rather than folded into SU-CP-15 (Autonomic Nervous System Physiology and Pharmacology).
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk. Flagged for coordinator awareness that Toronto Notes' own printed TOC layout occasionally nests a thematically-unrelated heading under a preceding section purely for column-space/typesetting reasons rather than genuine hierarchy - study-unit derivation should continue to prioritize confirmed body-heading structure and thematic coherence over raw TOC indentation, consistent with existing protocol guidance.

items.title: No dedicated MCC 'clinical pharmacology principles' objective
items.summary: 16 of this chapter's 20 study units (13 of 17 total OBJECTIVE_REFERENCE citations) anchor on the single MCC objective 125 'Prescribing practices', because it is the only Medical Expert objective dedicated to safe/individualized prescribing broadly. However, 125's own enabling-objectives text does not name specific PK/PD mechanisms (bioavailability, volume of distribution, half-life, CYP-mediated metabolism, receptor agonism/antagonism, therapeutic index) verbatim - the mapping_rationale on each affected unit (e.g. SU-CP-04 through SU-CP-11) honestly documents this as a MODERATE-strength inference from 125's broader risk-benefit/comorbidity/genetics language rather than a verbatim match.
items.resolution_status: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk - every affected unit still achieves at least MODERATE mapping_strength with a defensible textual anchor (0 WEAK mappings in this chapter).
items.recommended_action: Flagged for coordinator awareness in case future MCC objectives_registry.json updates add a more granular pharmacology-principles objective, or in case other chapters (e.g., Medicine's own therapeutics content, Psychiatry's psychopharmacology sections) encounter the same single-objective concentration and a cross-chapter registry annotation would help distribute evidence more precisely.

The remaining 7 are represented as SU-D-02, SU-D-03, SU-D-13, SU-D-14, SU-D-34, SU-D-45, SU-D-46, and folded into SU-D-48 (Landmark Trials). See study_units.json's unresolved_heading_resolution field for the complete per-heading resolution.

items.title: Unusually high rate of two-column TOC node-title merges (~20 of 42 nodes)
items.summary: Beyond the 9 fully-dropped headings above, roughly 20 of chapter D's 42 toc_inventory.json nodes carry titles that concatenate two real, physically distant headings that happened to share a TOC line during OCR (e.g. D.S06's title 'Cysts Malignant Skin Tumours' merges a pdf-196 subsection with a pdf-228 major heading 32 pages away). This is a substantially higher merge rate than any previously completed chapter (C, ELOM, A, CP).
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED for all 20 nodes - each was split into its constituent real fragments via body-heading confirmation, with the full per-node ledger recorded in study_units.json's same_page_merge_resolutions field. No mapping-quality impact: source_accounting passed with 0 unaccounted nodes and 0 WEAK mcc_evidence citations resulted.
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter D itself (fully resolved). Flagged informational so the coordinator is aware that chapter D's toc_inventory.json node titles are less reliable as literal section titles than other chapters if they are ever consumed directly (e.g. by tooling) rather than through study_units.json's resolved titles.

items.title: Section-boundary page numbers lag their true body content by one page for pdf 285-290
items.summary: For the contiguous run of toc_inventory.json nodes ER.S04 (tail)/ER.S05/ER.S06/ER.S07/ER.S08 (Otolaryngological, Gynecologic, Ophthalmologic, Dermatologic Emergencies), each node's recorded start_pdf_page is one page earlier than where its titled content actually begins in body OCR: ER.S05 states start_pdf_page 285 but pdf 285 body text is Stroke/TIA (belongs to ER.S04.T12); Epistaxis (ER.S05.T01) actually starts pdf 286 (inside ER.S06's stated range); Nephrolithiasis (ER.S06.T03) actually starts pdf 288 (inside ER.S07's stated range); Ophthalmologic content actually starts pdf 289 (inside ER.S08's stated range); Dermatologic content is a single real page at pdf 290 against a stated 289-290 range. This is a distinct defect class from the two-column TOC-OCR title merges documented elsewhere in this chapter - it affects page-boundary numbers on already-correctly-titled nodes, not the titles themselves.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED for chapter ER's own crosswalk - all 6 affected study units (SU-ER-28 through SU-ER-33) cite the toc_inventory.json node whose title is the correct structural match, but record the true confirmed pdf_page_range from body-heading confirmation rather than the node's stated range, with page_mapping_precision set to SECTION_INHERITED and the discrepancy noted in structural_rationale.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator should consider a targeted re-run or manual correction of the TOC-extraction pipeline's page-boundary assignment for chapter ER nodes S05-S08 in toc_inventory.json (shift each node's start_pdf_page/end_pdf_page forward by one page), since this is a distinct, previously undocumented class of extraction defect that could plausibly recur in other chapters with similar TOC layouts. Flagged informational/low-priority since chapter ER's own crosswalk is unaffected (all 6 units are fully resolved and validated against confirmed body pages).

If real content exists (especially 'Spinal Cord Trauma', which would otherwise leave MCC objective 109-13 under-represented in this chapter despite Traumatology being ER.S02's core content), it was not locatable within this chapter's declared pdf 247-308 page range via body-heading confirmation.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator should check whether a genuine 'Spinal Cord Trauma' subsection exists in the source PDF near ER.S02 (Traumatology, pdf 253-263) or ER.S11 (pdf 302) that this pass's page-by-page body scan missed, and whether 'Joint Pain' / 'Shortness of Breath' are genuine TOC entries for a different chapter (Rheumatology/Orthopedic Surgery for Joint Pain; Respirology for Shortness of Breath) that bled into ER's TOC OCR due to physical page adjacency in the printed book.

items.recommended_action: Coordinator/reviewer to confirm no MCC objective covers environmental heat illness before accepting zero MCC-linked question coverage for this content; if genuinely absent from MCC's objective set, this should be documented as a confirmed scope gap rather than left as an open search TODO.

items.title: E.S03.T02 / E.S03.T03 is one heading split by OCR line-wrap, not two topics
items.summary: The TOC extraction pass parsed the single heading 'Pre-Diabetes (Impaired Glucose Tolerance/Impaired Fasting Glucose)' into two topic nodes (E.S03.T02 title truncates mid-phrase at 'Impaired Fasting'; E.S03.T03 is the orphaned closing fragment 'Glucose)'), because the heading text wrapped across two lines on the TOC page. This differs from Dermatology's two-column merges (which combine two unrelated distant headings); here it is the same single heading split in two.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED - confirmed via body-heading OCR (clean-ocr/0315.txt, pdf 315) as one continuous Pre-Diabetes subsection and merged into a single study unit (SU-E-08).
items.recommended_action: Coordinator may want a line-wrap-aware post-processing pass on TOC extraction (join two adjacent unanchored topic nodes when the second node's title has no capital-letter start / looks like a sentence continuation) to prevent this class of artifact in future chapters, though the rate is very low (1 of 81 nodes in this chapter).

items.title: MCC objectives registry has no dedicated objective for several high-yield endocrine topics
items.summary: Full-registry keyword searches (search-mcc-objectives) for 'thyroid disease' subtypes beyond the general neck-mass objective, 'adrenal', 'Cushing', 'pituitary', 'hypogonadism', 'gynecomastia', 'hirsutism', 'osteoporosis', 'goiter/goitre', and several other core endocrinology terms returned zero matches. This is a genuine registry coverage gap, not a search-tooling failure (confirmed by successfully finding adjacent/related objectives like Hyperglycemia=130, Hypertension=9-1, Fatigue=33, Breast masses and enlargement=10-1 via the same search method).
items.resolution_status: RESOLVED FOR THIS CHAPTER - affected units (e.g. thyroid-specific diagnoses under objective 63 'Neck masses and thyroid disease'; Cushing's/pheochromocytoma/primary aldosteronism under objective 9-1 'Hypertension'; adrenal insufficiency under objective 33 'Fatigue'; gynecomastia under objective 10-1 'Breast masses and enlargement') were mapped as COMPONENT or DIRECT (where the objective's own text explicitly names the mechanism) under the nearest genuinely-matching presentation-based objective, with mapping_strength never exceeding what the objective's actual text supports. See crosswalk_audit.md's 'MCC registry search note' for the full list of 12 additional objectives found beyond the scope packet's bounded candidate set, and the full list of confirmed zero-match search terms.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator may want to flag this as a broader MCC-objectives-registry gap worth noting in the final scope-scaling report: several highly-tested Endocrinology topics (thyroid disease subtypes, adrenal disorders, pituitary disorders, osteoporosis) rely entirely on adjacent presentation-based objectives rather than a dedicated endocrine objective, which may be a pattern in other body-system chapters (e.g. Cardiology, Gastroenterology) worth checking when those are processed.
